quote: Assumption 3.1. Suppose {X_1, · · · , X_n} [{Y_1, · · · , Y_n}] are n interdependent variables coupled with Archimedean (survival) copula with generator ψ_1 [ψ_2], where, for i = 1, · · · , n, X_i ∼ Kw-G(x, α_i, γ_i; G) [Y_i ∼ Kw-G(x, β_i, δ_i; H)] and G [H] is the baseline distribution function. Further, let N_1 [N_2] be a positive integer-valued random variable independently of X'_i [Y'_i]. Also, let us denote r_g(x) = G'(x)/Ḡ(x) and r_h(x) = H'(x)/H̄(x). We start this section by the following theorem which states that under some sufficient conditions, if α ⪰^w β, then the random maxima X_{N_1:N_1} is stochastically larger than Y_{N_2:N_2}. Theorem 3.1. Let Assumption 3.1 hold with α, β ∈ E_+(D_+), γ = δ(≥ 1_n), G ≤ H . Also, suppose ϕ_2 ∘ ψ_1 is super-additive and ψ_1 or ψ_2 is log-concave. Then, α ⪰^w β ⇒ X_{N_1:N_1} ≥_st Y_{N_2:N_2}, whenever N_1 ≤_st N_2.

quote: Next, we consider a counterexample to show that the condition ψ_1 or ψ_2 is log-concave plays a crucial role for the result in Theorem 3.1 to hold. Counterexample 3.1. Let, X_i ∼ Kw-G(x, α_i, γ_i; G) and Y_i ∼ Kw-G(x, β_i, γ_i; H), for i = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Set (γ_1, γ_2, γ_3, γ_4, γ_5) = (1.2, 1.5, 1.9, 2, 2.1), (α_1, α_2, α_3, α_4, α_5) = (1.1, 0.001, 0.0001, 0.00001, 0.00001) and (β_1, β_2, β_3, β_4, β_5) = (2.1, 3.001, 5.0001, 0.001, 0.0001). Clearly, (α_1, α_2, α_3, α_4, α_5) ⪰^w (β_1, β_2, β_3, β_4, β_5). Let G(x) = e^{−1/x} and H(x) = 1 − e^{−x}, for x > 0. Also, let (X_1, X_2, X_3) be selected with probability P(N_1 = 3) = p(3) = 1/5, (X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4) be selected with probability P(N_1 = 4) = p(4) = 2/5 and, (X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4, X_5) be selected with probability P(N_1 = 5) = p(5) = 2/5; further let (Y_1, Y_2, Y_3) be selected with probability P(N_2 = 3) = p(3) = 1/5, (Y_1, Y_2, Y_3, Y_4) be selected with probability P(N_2 = 4) = p(4) = 3/5 and (Y_1, Y_2, Y_3, Y_4, Y_5) be selected with probability P(N_2 = 5) = p(5) = 1/5. Suppose X_i ∼ Kw-G(x, α_i, γ_i; G) and Y_i ∼ Kw-G(x, α_i, δ_i; H), for i = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
